newsitem.title: UK: New Armenian air cargo terminal to be ready in Nov.
newsitem.headline: New Armenian air cargo terminal to be ready in Nov.

text.p: The new airport cargo handling unit at Armenia's capital of Yerevan, should be completed by around November this year, Vahram Avanessian, Minister of Economy, told Reuters on Sunday at the Annual General Meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

The Armenian delegation earlier told an EBRD seminar that while the new $27.8 million cargo facility was well underway and should be ready by October, other upgrading such as the control tower and operations control systems were still being tackled.

They said this would cost around $3 million but they were still searching for investment credits from companies to cover the remaining $2 million dollars after the French government gave a grant of around $1 million for work to be done by Thomson of France.

Avanessian said the new cargo unit would be able to offer specialist handling for 60,000 tonnes a year. He said cargo handled in 1992 was 120,000 tonnes which had dropped to around 40,000 tonnes a year by the end of 1995.

"For the year 1996, I think the figure would be less. I think...I hope, that the figure should be climbing now but it is not easy to estimate," he added as much of the cargo was coming through via commercial tourism.
Tourists make trips abroad to buy consumer goods, textiles and leather wear and bring them back as excess or unaccompanied "baggage" to resell in Armenia and throughout the former Soviet Union.

An individual might bring a 100 kg or more back in this way on each trip. The minister said official cargo statistics in states across the former Soviet Union were unable to take this very significant traffic into account.
